reason: I'll follow the broken icy moon fragments and their encounter with slow rubble, addressing the second goal.

alternatives.reason: The icy moonlets and dust could advance the close-moon story, but I chose to follow the existing fragments first.

effect: The fragments have gathered beyond the disruptive inner region, so I can follow their next encounter.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the broken moon's material remain bound together.
reason: I'll follow the outer gathering into its encounter with the crossing stones.

reaction: The contrast between gathering farther out and disruption near the giant is interesting.
reason: I'll combine the ice-rich moonlets with dust; it's the only offered combination and should advance the remaining goal.

reaction: Its loose structure makes me curious how the impact will change it.
reason: The impact is the only offered combination and should advance the close-moon path.

effect: The impact redirected the surviving rubble moon toward the giant, making the close encounter the next step.
reaction: The orbital change is more interesting than a simple breakup.
reason: The giant encounter is the only offered combination and follows the remaining goal.
expectation: The giant's tidal pull may break up the weakly bound moon, potentially leaving orbiting debris.

effect: The giant's tidal pull broke up the close-passing moon, producing rings and completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The contrast with the fragments that formed an outer moon made the ring formation satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: The close encounter was most worthwhile: it showed why loose material can remain dispersed in rings near the giant while similar fragments gathered farther out.

leastWorthwhile.text: Sweeping dust into the moonlet felt like a relatively routine buildup compared with the subsequent orbital change.

surprise.text: The head-on impact redirected the surviving rubble moon toward the giant rather than simply breaking it apart.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the dust buildup had a clear purpose, even if it was less interesting.

continue.text: Yes. The contrasting fates of similar material made me curious about what happens next in the system.
